essence: The conduct-septad remembered in the heart; the abode entered again; the discussion itself known — it names its own close.

sections.SUMMARY: The conduct-septad remembered in the heart; the abode entered again; the discussion itself known — it names its own close.
sections.FUNCTION: Establishes remembered, entered, known — the ending.
sections.KEY TERMS:
* **sadvṛtta** — good conduct
* **saptaka** — septad
* **galita** — dissolved
* **anyacintā** — other thoughts
* **samyak** — rightly
* **smaranti** — remember
* **hṛdaya** — heart
* **paramārthakāma** — desiring the ultimate
* **bhairavīya** — Bhairava's one
* **paradhāman** — supreme abode
* **muhuḥ** — again
* **viśanti** — enter
* **jānanti** — know
* **trijagatīparamārthacarcā** — three-worlds' ultimate-thing-discussion
sections.EXPLANATION: This (idam) septad (saptakam) of good conduct (sadvṛtta) — those whose other (anya) thoughts (cintāḥ) are dissolved (galitā), desiring the ultimate (paramārthakāmāḥ), rightly (samyak) remember (smaranti) it in the heart (hṛdaye): conduct remembered inwardly, not performed outwardly. Those (te) — O Bhairava's one (bhairavīya, vocative address) — again (muhuḥ) enter (viśanti) the supreme abode (paradhāma), and (ca) know (jānanti) the ultimate-thing-discussion (paramārthacarcām) of the three worlds (trijagatī). Entering, then knowing: the abode first, its discussion after. It names itself at the ending — those who enter know this very discussion.
sections.BOUNDARY: Whether 'bhairavīya' is vocative address or genitive is unresolved.
sections.RELATED: * Paramārthacarcā v.1 — light needs no lamp.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is knowledge (jñāna) in the mode of close (nigamana); the vyabhicāri is peace (śānti) of conduct remembered.
